amendments.change: Adjudication mode changed from blind solo human adjudication to AI-drafted, human-confirmed. An independent agent session drafts all 140 cases from blind inputs (descriptions, sections, all same-section definitions; no expected labels, no classifier picks). The operator then confirms or edits every case in the page; a case counts as done only after confirmation.
amendments.reason: The user chose this mode to reduce adjudication effort while keeping a human decision on every case. Provenance will record the draft explicitly: the frozen reference states ai_drafted true with the draft file's SHA-256. Validity is weaker than blind independent human adjudication (confirmation-anchoring risk); the summary says so. Blindness to the original AI reference and to classifier picks is preserved because the drafting session never sees them.

amendments.change: Added a judge round on top of the AI draft: an independent second agent labelled all 140 cases blind; the drafting agent reconsidered the 16 disagreements and issued final positions (9 keep, 6 concede, 1 other). The confirm page now pre-selects the post-reconsideration label, badges the 130 two-agent-agreed cases for fast confirmation, and flags the 10 still-disputed cases for the operator's closest attention. The judge verdicts and reconsideration files are pinned by SHA-256 in the frozen reference.
amendments.reason: The user ran the judge and reconsideration rounds in separate sessions to strengthen the AI draft before confirming. Every case still requires an operator decision; the additional rounds are recorded as agent evidence, never as the outcome.
amendments.recorded_before: rebuilding the confirm page with the consensus layer

amendments.change: The operator confirmed by in-session instruction instead of the per-case page pass: all 10 still-disputed cases take the judge's label, and the 130 two-agent consensus cases are accepted wholesale. Because the judge agreed with the draft on 124 and the conceded 6 already carry the judge's label, the frozen reference equals the judge's 140 labels. corpus/adjudication-decisions.json was generated from that instruction, not from a page download.
amendments.reason: Operator's explicit choice after reviewing the dispute summary. Provenance records it as batch confirmation: the 10 hardest cases received individual human arbitration; the 124 two-agent-agreed cases carry no individual human review. The validity note states this; it is weaker than the per-case page confirmation the page was built for.

amendments.change: Fixed a verify-path bug in finalise_reference.py (the recomputed summary lacked the manifest_digest key the written summary carries), then re-froze the reference. The decisions, inputs and every recorded value are unchanged; only the runner SHA-256 in the binding manifest moved.
amendments.reason: The first freeze used the pre-fix runner, so the fingerprint no longer matched. Re-freeze reproduces the identical reference content under the fixed runner; agreement and re-score outputs are unchanged.

amendments.change: Independent review findings fixed: verify now also checks the frozen reference against plan.json's reference_sha256 pin (metadata tampering fails); the consensus builder derives agreement from draft and judge labels and rejects an agree flag inconsistent with them; the page's confirm handler no longer references an undeclared variable. The reference was re-frozen because finalise_reference.py's runner SHA-256 changed.
amendments.reason: Review hardening. Decisions, inputs and all recorded values are unchanged; agreement and re-score outputs are identical.
amendments.recorded_before: re-freezing the reference after the review round

decision_rule: Freeze the adjudicated file as the trusted reference either way. Use the disagreement rate and the re-scored Experiment 06 metrics to decide whether the Experiment 05, 06 and 09 conclusions need revisiting, and to drive the catalogue consolidation experiment.

agent_draft.contamination_rule: the drafting session reads only the blind input file; it must not read ground-truth, experiment outputs or reports
agent_draft.input: corpus/agent-input-blind.json (descriptions, sections, all same-section definitions; no expected labels)

judge_round.design: an independent judge labelled all 140 cases blind; the drafter reconsidered the 16 disagreements; the page pre-selects the post-reconsideration label and badges each case as agents-agree (settled) or disputed (needs the operator most)

adjudication.mode: AI-drafted, human-confirmed: an independent agent session drafts every case from blind inputs; the operator confirms or edits each case in the page; no AI reference, classifier pick or expected label is ever shown
adjudication.options: every same-section label (22 preferences or 19 patterns), none_fit, uncertain
adjudication.page: output/adjudication.html; offline single file; consensus pre-selected per case (draft, revised by the reconsideration round); a case counts as done only after the operator confirms or changes it; autosave in localStorage; one JSON download
adjudication.uncertain_handling: kept in the frozen reference; excluded from re-score rates; counted separately
